name: A01: Broken Access Control
evidence: Authenticated routes expose resource-scoped identifiers such as /api/Users/:id, /api/Cards/:id, /api/Addresss/:id, and /rest/basket/:id.

name: A02: Cryptographic Failures
evidence: The application has password login, password reset/change flows, JWT-related dependencies, 2FA, cards, wallet data, and encryption-key serving functionality.

name: A03: Injection
evidence: The summary reports no raw SQL queries, no MongoDB usage, and no identified eval/exec or interpolated query construction.

name: A04: Insecure Design
evidence: The architecture contains sensitive business flows and numerous public or weakly protected routes, but design-level security flaws cannot be established reliably from route inventory alone.

name: A05: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: XML parsing, CORS, static file serving, public FTP, API documentation, and security-header dependencies are present, but parser hardening, CORS policy, and effective header configuration are not shown.

name: A06: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
evidence: The application has 117 dependencies, including security-sensitive components such as express-jwt, jsonwebtoken, multer, js-yaml, libxml2-wasm, and Sequelize.

name: A07: Identification and Authentication Failures
evidence: Login, password change/reset, security-question, JWT authorization, 2FA, and rate-limited authentication-related endpoints are present.

name: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
evidence: The application processes uploaded YAML/XML files and includes webhook handling, deserialization/parsing libraries, and restore-progress/data-import style functionality.

name: A09: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
evidence: A logging module, metrics middleware, and public /metrics endpoints are present, establishing logging and monitoring functionality that requires security assessment.

name: A10: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
evidence: The application exposes a profile image URL upload route, indicating server-side retrieval of caller-supplied URLs.

name: API1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
evidence: The REST/API surface contains many ID-based resources, including users, baskets, cards, addresses, products, memories, and orders.

name: API2: Broken Authentication
evidence: The API includes login, reset-password, change-password, JWT authorization, 2FA, and user identity endpoints.

name: API3: Broken Object Property Level Authorization
evidence: Twenty-eight auto-CRUD routes expose model objects with broad property sets and no custom hooks; only limited attributes are explicitly excluded for users.

name: API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption
evidence: The API supports file uploads, pagination, search, AI chat, image processing, bulk-style CRUD operations, and resource-intensive flows; rate limiting is only visible on selected endpoints.

name: API5: Broken Function Level Authorization
evidence: The API contains administrative, accounting, wallet, order, user, and CRUD functions with inconsistent authorization coverage, including many routes marked auth:null.

name: API6: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
evidence: Sensitive flows include password reset, checkout, coupon application, wallet funding, deluxe membership, file uploads, data export, and order operations.

name: API7: Server Side Request Forgery
evidence: The profile image URL upload route provides a structural server-side URL-fetching capability.

name: API8: Security Misconfiguration
evidence: The API has extensive undocumented hand-written and auto-CRUD routes, public file-serving surfaces, public metrics, and inconsistent authorization declarations.

name: API9: Improper Inventory Management
evidence: Swagger documents only one path while 109 hand-written routes and 28 auto-CRUD routes are undocumented.

name: API10: Unsafe Consumption of APIs
evidence: The system consumes external or provider-backed capabilities through the AI SDK/OpenAI-compatible integration, web3 functionality, and URL-based image handling.

name: LLM01: Prompt Injection
evidence: A chatbot endpoint uses a genuine LLM with user-supplied prompts and multi-step tool execution.

name: LLM02: Sensitive Information Disclosure
evidence: LLM tools can query products, reviews, and orders and perform authentication checks against real application data.

name: LLM03: Supply Chain
evidence: The application depends on AI SDK and OpenAI-compatible provider components that participate in production LLM functionality.

name: LLM05: Improper Output Handling
evidence: The application has extensive Angular innerHTML and bypassSecurityTrustHtml usage, but the summary does not establish that LLM output reaches these sinks without validation.

name: LLM06: Excessive Agency
evidence: The LLM has multi-step tool calling with real capabilities including database queries, authentication checks, order retrieval, and coupon generation.

name: LLM10: Unbounded Consumption
evidence: A public chat endpoint supports streaming and multi-step tool execution, with no explicit chat-specific rate, token, step, or cost limits shown.
